text: The power spiked to many times its normal level, in a few seconds. Fuel shattered, water flashed into steam, and the pressure burst the fuel channels. The rods jammed, partway in. A steam explosion threw the reactor's massive steel lid, weighing at least a thousand tonnes, up through the roof. Seconds later, a second explosion scattered burning graphite and fuel across the site. The graphite burned for days, and the smoke carried radioactive material across Europe. Two workers died that night. Dozens more died from radiation in the months that followed, and the long-term toll is still debated.
